OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$, there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.
#173: [Er75f,p.108][ErGr79][ErGr80][Er83c]
geometry | 
ramsey theory
For some colourings a single equilateral triangle has to be excluded, considering the colouring by alternating strips. Shader [Sh76] has proved this is true if we just consider a single right-angled triangle.

Original paper that answers the question for several familieas of triangles: [Erdos, P., Graham, R. L., Montgomery, P., Rothschild, B. L., Spencer, J., & Straus, E. G. Euclidean Ramsey theorems 3, (1975)].

Recent progress: [Currier, Gabriel, Kenneth Moore, and Chi Hoi Yip. "Any two-coloring of the plane contains monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions." Combinatorica 44.6 (2024): 1367-1380.]
Upper bounds: [Mundinger, K., Zimmer, M., Kiem, A., Spiegel, C., & Pokutta, S. (2025). Neural Discovery in Mathematics: Do Machines Dream of Colored Planes?. arXiv preprint arXiv:2501.18527.]
